messages.subject: Estimating DIF for a multi-group multi-dimensional model w/highly correlated latent parameters
parts:
Hi mirters,

I'm trying to estimate a multi-group multi-dimensional model w/highly correlated latent parameters. My model includes five indicators: three on one latent, two on another. I realize that this model is just barely identified, and that this sounds like a situation that calls for a unidimensional model. And I am interested in a unidimensional model, but I need to estimation both the uni and multi models. For the sake of this post, please trust that I have good reasons to test the two-factor model, so it's important for me to be able to properly estimate and parameterize. 

Unsurprisingly, the multidimensional model has difficulty converging. I read on another post by Dr. Chalmers that I should try to use the method = "MHRM" argument, because the stochastic estimation procedure of MHRM makes it less susceptible to model failure in my situation. That worked: I was able to estimate the model, and run DIF tests on the items using the DIF() function in mirt!

Now here's the problem. All of the multidimensional DIF tests came back indicating DIF. But when I estimated a unidimensional model based on the same items using the EM estimator, the DIF tests came back indicating the items are non-DIF. And the difference between the DIF results for the two models was enormous - chi squared values for the uni model were roughly < 10 on 7 df, but for the multi dimensional model they were > 100. And here's the kicker: when I went back and re-estimated the unidimensional model using method = "MHRM" argument, I got the same results as the multidimensional model, indicating that the items are all DIF. 

I should say I also have good reason to expect these items are probably non-DIF, because MI tests in the CFA framework (using the fixed-factor method) based on both the uni and multi models indicate that the models are invariant. That's data-driven evidence that the items might be invariant. It is imperfect evidence, but makes me skeptical that my items are all DIF

Take together, this set of results makes me think DIF results for the multidimensional model appear to be an artifact of the MHRM estimation, rather than being truly DIF (however, this statement assume that EM is globally more valid than MHRM). My primary question is, Is there a better way to estimate the multidimensional model to get appropriate DIF results? I am not fishing for a way to get non-DIF: if the items are DIF, then so be it. But right now I don't trust the results of the method = "MHRM" estimation technique.

Here is the code for the multidimensional model I'm trying to run, as well as a print out of the item parameters and DIF results:

### Two-factor model


# Two factor model syntax
dddTwoFactorIRTSyntax <- mirt.model(
'
symp = 1-3
tend = 4-5
COV = symp*tend
'
)


# Unrestrained two-factor multiple group model
ddd.model.multi.free <- mirt::multipleGroup(data = dddMirtData,
                                            model = dddTwoFactorIRTSyntax,
                                            itemtype = "graded",
                                            group = dddata$SexCode,
                                            method = "MHRM")


# Coefficients for the unrestrained two-factor multiple group model
coef(ddd.model.multi.free,
     simplify = TRUE)


# Constrain the model
ddd.constrained.multi.model <- mirt::multipleGroup(data = dddMirtData,
                                                   model = dddTwoFactorIRTSyntax,
                                                   itemtype = "graded",
                                                   group = dddata$SexCode,
                                                   invariance = c(colnames(dddMirtData),
                                                                  'free_means',
                                                                  'free_var'),
                                                   method = "MHRM")


# Constrain the parameters
ddd.constrained.multi.parameters <- coef(ddd.constrained.multi.model,
                                        simplify = TRUE)[[1]][[1]]


# First round of AOAA selection.
ddd.dif.drop.multi <- DIF(ddd.constrained.multi.model,
                          c('a1',
                            'a2',
                            'd1',
                            'd2',
                            'd3',
                            'd4',
                            'd5',
                            'd6'),
                          scheme = 'drop',
                          seq_stat = .05,
                          method = "MHRM")


## use the optional function to table the output
get.dif.items(f.data=ddd.dif.drop.multi,
              p.val=.05,
              parms=ddd.constrained.multi.parameters)

Hi Thomas,

It sounds like you've encountered a strange edge-case situation where even the ML estimation algorithms are at odds (which is not a great sign...). I checked that the procedure is performing as expected (see simulation code below), so I can only assume this is due to problematic data conditions with your dataset. Specifically, I can see unusually high slope parameters, indicating effectively step-functions (bad news), as well as extreme intercept locations, indicating very sparse cell counts (also bad news). The MHRM may be just masking things in this case as the MHRM really should only outperform the EM algorithm in cases when numerical integration becomes inaccurate (which, with two latent traits, shouldn't be the case), so it's likely the baseline model supplied to DIF() is rather far from a stable MLE location, and therefore relative comparisons based on likelihood criteria could in reference to an improper base model. I am speculating a little, but this seems the most likely case. HTH.

Phil

---------------

library(mirt)

a <- matrix(c(rlnorm(3, .2, .2), numeric(5), rlnorm(2, .2, .2)), ncol=2)
diffs <- t(apply(matrix(runif(5*7, .3, 1), 5), 1, cumsum))
diffs <- -(diffs - rowMeans(diffs))
d <- diffs + rnorm(5)
r <- .9

cov1 <- matrix(c(1,r,r,1), 2)
cov2 <- matrix(c(1.5,r,r,.9), 2)

means1 <- c(0,0)
means2 <- c(.5,.7)

dat1 <- simdata(a, d, 500, itemtype = 'graded', sigma = cov1, mu = means1)
dat2 <- simdata(a, d, 500, itemtype = 'graded', sigma = cov2, mu = means2)

group <- rep(c('G1', 'G2'), each=500)
dddMirtData <- rbind(dat1, dat2)

### Two-factor model
# Two factor model syntax
dddTwoFactorIRTSyntax <- mirt.model(
    '
symp = 1-3
tend = 4-5
COV = symp*tend
'
)


# Unrestrained two-factor multiple group model
ddd.model.multi.free <- mirt::multipleGroup(data = dddMirtData,
                                            model = dddTwoFactorIRTSyntax,
                                            itemtype = "graded",

# group = dddata$SexCode,
                                            group = group,

method = "MHRM")


# Coefficients for the unrestrained two-factor multiple group model
coef(ddd.model.multi.free,
     simplify = TRUE)


# Constrain the model
ddd.constrained.multi.model <- mirt::multipleGroup(data = dddMirtData,
                                                   model = dddTwoFactorIRTSyntax,
                                                   itemtype = "graded",

# group = dddata$SexCode,
                                                   group = group,

invariance = c(colnames(dddMirtData),
                                                                  'free_means',
                                                                  'free_var'),
                                                   method = "MHRM")


# Constrain the parameters
ddd.constrained.multi.parameters <- coef(ddd.constrained.multi.model,
                                         simplify = TRUE)[[1]][[1]]


# First round of AOAA selection.
ddd.dif.drop.multi <- DIF(ddd.constrained.multi.model,
                          c('a1',
                            'a2',
                            'd1',
                            'd2',
                            'd3',
                            'd4',
                            'd5',
                            'd6'),
                          scheme = 'drop',
                          seq_stat = .05,
